subject: Re: Intermittent uptime variance — remediation & premium path discussion
body:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueharbor.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Intermittent uptime variance — saw multiple short dips this week

Hi Alex / Laura,

Quick note from our SRE team: we observed three short dips in availability on 2026-06-11 and increased 95/99th tail latency for several endpoints between 02:00-03:30 UTC. Attachments include the raw traces and the aggregated deltas. This has started to impact a subset of trading jobs during morning opening; our ops team is asking what remediation looks like and whether an SLA uplift or credits are possible while we explore a longer-term fix.

Can we get an estimated timeline for an RCA and a proposed immediate mitigation (we can run a pilot of anything that helps reduce tail latency)? Also: renewal is coming up in September — our CFO wants to understand whether upgrading to a premium SLA tier would materially reduce these events and what the commercial delta would be.

Attachments: uptime-delta-log-20260611.zip (log bundle, 12MB)

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, BlueHarbor Financial
samir.patel@blueharbor.com

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. We take any uptime variance seriously. Immediate plan below:

1) Triage call: propose a 45-minute runbook call Monday 2026-06-15 14:00 UTC to review traces and correlate with our routing/fallbacks. Laura, Marissa — can you join?
2) Short mitigation: we can enable a temporary priority routing and prefix KV-cache warm for the affected endpoints to reduce tail latency while we investigate. This is low-risk and reversible.
3) RCA + remediation: we'll deliver an initial RCA by end of day Thursday (2026-06-18) with a recommended remediation plan.
4) Commercial: we can outline the premium SLA uplift options and what delta in availability/credits to expect — I will send a commercial sketch after the triage.

I attached an initial remediation outline (short bullets) to share with ops; Marissa will fill in technical options after the triage.

Attachments: initial-remediation-plan.pdf

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueharbor.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent uptime variance — saw multiple short dips this week

Thanks for the session earlier — good context. A few technical notes from triage and a short remediation checklist:

Observations:
- Correlated spikes at ~02:05 UTC and ~03:10 UTC align with a background batch job window from BlueHarbor (Samir confirmed). The sequence-length distribution shifted upward for requests hitting the larger LLM variant, which pushed kernel selection to a slower path under bursting conditions.
- KV cache warm misses contributed to extra token-level latency for mid-sequence requests.

Short remediation checklist (can be applied as a pilot):
1) Route sensitive production routes to a quantized, lower-memory model variant for the 02:00-04:00 UTC window — reduces median and tail latency with minimal quality delta for these request types. (Risk: 3/10)
2) Enable prefix KV cache pre-warm for the observed prefixes + a short TTL-based extension during the morning window. (Risk: 2/10)
3) Temporary rate smoothing for non-critical background batch jobs — throttle to keep sustained concurrency below kernel threshold. (Risk: 4/10)

Estimated impact: combined, we expect 60-80% reduction in 99th-percentile token latency for the affected window; availability dips should be eliminated for the majority of requests. We'll instrument metrics and provide a verification dashboard during the pilot.

I can push the pilot config to a dedicated pool tonight; would need BlueHarbor ops approval to change routing and throttle batch jobs.

Marissa Cole
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: none

Alex / Team — thanks for the quick triage and the proposed pilot. A few items from finance/Procurement:

1) Pilot approval: ops is fine with the temporary routing and cache warm. Please share the exact configuration and rollback playbook.
2) Credits: given the recent availability impact, we'd like to understand the credit mechanics for incidents that trigger the current SLA. Is there a path to expedited credit processing while we run the pilot?
3) Premium tier: our renewal conversations start mid-July. We need a clear before/after comparison: what does the premium SLA guarantee versus our current plan (availability numbers, latency SLOs, credits, escalation windows) and the expected commercial delta. Can you send a simple one-page comparison and a ballpark uplift cost we can share with the CFO?

Also attaching a short ops export of the trading-job impact for your reference.

Attachments: trading-impact-summary.csv

Regards,
Maria Lopez
VP Finance (acting), BlueHarbor Financial
maria.lopez@blueharbor.com

Maria / Samir — appreciate the clear asks. Summary of next steps and deliverables:

Deliverables by EOD Monday 2026-06-21:
- Pilot config + rollback playbook (Marissa)
- Verification dashboard + expected verification metrics (Marissa)
- One-page commercial comparison: current vs premium SLA (availability, 95/99 latency goals, credits cadence, escalation response) and a ballpark uplift (Alex)
- Draft commercial offer for premium tier and estimated time-to-implementation for onramp (Alex)

Commercial note (preview): upgrading to our Premium SLA includes a tighter availability target (99.99% vs 99.9%), formal tail-latency SLOs at the 95/99 token-level, 24/7 triage with a named on-call, and a defined credit schedule that is faster to process. Ballpark uplift for a customer with BlueHarbor's profile is ~20-28% over current run-rate; I will include a precise number in the Monday package.

Attached: commercial-offer-BH.pdf (draft sketch — non-binding). We will not change any billing until we align on the SLOs and pilot results.

Can we set a follow-up to review the commercial sketch on Tuesday 2026-06-22 15:00 UTC (30 minutes)? If so I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to stabilizing this quickly.

Best,
Alex Martinez
